exercises.name: Barbell bench press
exercises.why: The most studied chest builder; easy to load and progress for years, but it costs more fatigue than machines.

exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
exercises.why: Dumbbells let the elbows travel lower, so the chest is loaded deeper into the stretch.

exercises.name: Machine chest press
exercises.why: A fixed path lets you push close to failure safely and add weight in small steps.

exercises.name: Smith bench press
exercises.why: Stable bar path keeps the effort on the chest instead of balancing the weight.

exercises.name: Weighted dip
exercises.why: Deep shoulder extension stretches the lower chest under heavy load, but it is hard on some shoulders.

exercises.name: Cable fly
exercises.why: Cables keep tension through the whole arc, including the stretched position.

exercises.name: Pec deck
exercises.why: Stable and easy to take to failure with very little systemic fatigue.

exercises.name: Deficit push-up
exercises.why: Push-ups taken close to failure have matched bench press for chest growth in studies; a deficit adds range.

exercises.name: Dumbbell fly
exercises.why: Big stretch at the bottom, but the load drops to almost nothing at the top.

exercises.name: Incline barbell press
exercises.why: A low incline shifts more work to the clavicular fibres without turning it into a shoulder press.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell press
exercises.why: Longer range than the barbell version, with a deeper stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Incline machine press
exercises.why: Stable and simple to progress in small weight jumps.

exercises.name: Incline Smith press
exercises.why: The fixed bar path lets you focus on effort rather than balance.

exercises.name: Low-to-high cable fly
exercises.why: The upward line of pull matches the direction of the upper chest fibres.

exercises.name: Incline cable fly
exercises.why: Constant cable tension with a good stretch on the upper chest.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell fly
exercises.why: Large stretch, but loading is light and fades near the top.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
exercises.why: Full overhead stretch and easy to load in small steps; studies show it grows the lats comparably to pull-ups.

exercises.name: Pull-up
exercises.why: Great stretch at the bottom; progression needs added weight once reps get high.

exercises.name: Single-arm cable pulldown
exercises.why: Working one side lets the arm reach further overhead for a longer stretch.

exercises.name: Assisted pull-up
exercises.why: Pull-up range of motion with load you can adjust in small steps.

exercises.name: Close-grip pulldown
exercises.why: A neutral close grip allows a long pull with the elbows near the body.

exercises.name: Straight-arm pulldown
exercises.why: Isolates the lats without the biceps limiting you; light and low fatigue.

exercises.name: Dumbbell pullover
exercises.why: Loads the lats with the arms overhead, though the tension shifts to the chest as well.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell row
exercises.why: Long range with the free hand bracing the torso.

exercises.name: Barbell row
exercises.why: Heavy compound pull, but lower-back fatigue limits how much volume you can do.

exercises.name: Chest-supported row
exercises.why: Chest support removes the lower back from the lift so the upper back can be trained hard.

exercises.name: Seated cable row
exercises.why: Reaching forward at the start gives a long stretch with steady cable tension.

exercises.name: T-bar row
exercises.why: Heavy and easy to load, with moderate lower-back demand.

exercises.name: Iso-lateral machine row
exercises.why: Easy to progress and safe to take to failure.

exercises.name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
exercises.why: Dumbbells on an incline bench allow a long range without lower-back strain.

exercises.name: Barbell row
exercises.why: Classic mass builder with a high fatigue cost.

exercises.name: Machine shrug
exercises.why: Direct work for the upper traps; heavy loads are simple to progress.

exercises.name: Reverse pec deck
exercises.why: Targets the rear delts and mid-traps with almost no fatigue.

exercises.name: Face pull
exercises.why: Good for shoulder health, a weak growth stimulus on its own.

exercises.name: Cable lateral raise
exercises.why: With the cable behind the body the side delts are loaded at the bottom, where dumbbells give nothing.

exercises.name: Machine lateral raise
exercises.why: A stable path and small weight steps make progression simple.

exercises.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
exercises.why: The most studied option, but there is almost no load in the bottom range.

exercises.name: Seated cable lateral raise
exercises.why: Sitting removes body swing so the cable tension stays on the delts.

exercises.name: Lying incline lateral raise
exercises.why: Lying on an incline moves the hardest point to the stretched position, but loads stay very light.

exercises.name: Wide-grip upright row
exercises.why: Heavier side-delt option that can bother some shoulders.

exercises.name: Machine shoulder press
exercises.why: Mostly front delts; the side delts get meaningful but secondary work.

exercises.name: Dumbbell shoulder press
exercises.why: Compound press with a slightly longer range than machines.

exercises.name: Reverse pec deck
exercises.why: Stable path and simple progression for direct rear-delt work.

exercises.name: Cable reverse fly
exercises.why: Crossed cables start each rep from a stretch and keep tension throughout.

exercises.name: Face pull
exercises.why: Trains the rear delts together with the external rotators.

exercises.name: Rope rear-delt row
exercises.why: Wide elbows bias the rear delts in a heavier rowing pattern.

exercises.name: Rear-delt barbell row
exercises.why: Heavy compound option, but lower-back fatigue adds up.

exercises.name: Lying rear-delt raise
exercises.why: Chest support removes momentum from the movement.

exercises.name: Bent-over reverse fly
exercises.why: Easy to cheat with momentum and hard to progress.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell curl
exercises.why: Arms behind the body stretch the long head while it is under load.

exercises.name: Machine preacher curl
exercises.why: Hardest near the bottom, where training at long lengths seems to help growth most.

exercises.name: EZ-bar preacher curl
exercises.why: Preacher curls are well studied and load the elbow flexors in the stretch.

exercises.name: Bayesian cable curl
exercises.why: The cable from behind keeps tension on the biceps in the stretched position.

exercises.name: Barbell curl
exercises.why: Easy to load and track over time; a staple in hypertrophy studies.

exercises.name: EZ-bar curl
exercises.why: Same as the barbell curl but kinder to the wrists.

exercises.name: Cable curl
exercises.why: Smooth tension through the range with small weight steps.

exercises.name: Chin-up
exercises.why: Compound pull with heavy biceps involvement.

exercises.name: Hammer curl
exercises.why: Shifts work toward the brachialis and brachioradialis.

exercises.name: Spider curl
exercises.why: Hardest at the top and easy in the stretch.

exercises.name: Overhead cable extension
exercises.why: Maeo et al. found overhead extensions grew the triceps more than pushdowns, likely from stretching the long head.

exercises.name: Overhead dumbbell extension
exercises.why: Same long-head stretch as the cable version, but awkward to load heavy.

exercises.name: Skull crusher
exercises.why: Lowering the bar behind the head adds stretch to the long head.

exercises.name: Close-grip bench press
exercises.why: Heavy compound press, easy to progress.

exercises.name: V-bar pushdown
exercises.why: Simple and low fatigue, but short on stretch for the long head.

exercises.name: Rope pushdown
exercises.why: Low-fatigue isolation with a slightly longer finish than a bar.

exercises.name: Dip
exercises.why: Heavy bodyweight press with strong triceps work.

exercises.name: Dip machine
exercises.why: Dip pattern with adjustable load and a stable path.

exercises.name: JM press
exercises.why: Hybrid of a press and an extension; heavy but technical.

exercises.name: Dumbbell kickback
exercises.why: Tension only at the top, with very light loads.

exercises.name: Hack squat
exercises.why: Deep knee bend under heavy load with the back supported.

exercises.name: Back squat (deep)
exercises.why: The most proven quad builder, but also the most tiring.

exercises.name: Pendulum squat
exercises.why: Very deep knee range with little spine load.

exercises.name: Leg press
exercises.why: Easy to load heavy and push close to failure safely.

exercises.name: Leg extension
exercises.why: The only way to fully train the rectus femoris; Pedrosa et al. found extra growth from emphasising the stretched range.

exercises.name: Smith squat
exercises.why: A fixed bar path lets you sit deep with less balance demand.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
exercises.why: Big quad and glute stretch, though balance limits the load.

exercises.name: Front squat
exercises.why: An upright torso shifts more work to the quads.

exercises.name: Sissy squat
exercises.why: Stretches the quads with the hips extended; hard to load.

exercises.name: Seated leg curl
exercises.why: Maeo et al. found seated curls grew the hamstrings more than lying curls because the flexed hip stretches them.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
exercises.why: Heavy load at long hamstring lengths, with a high fatigue cost.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
exercises.why: Same hip hinge as the barbell RDL, with grip as the usual limit.

exercises.name: Lying leg curl
exercises.why: Simple and low fatigue, but the extended hip shortens the hamstrings.

exercises.name: Stiff-leg deadlift
exercises.why: Like the RDL with a slightly longer range from the floor.

exercises.name: Standing leg curl
exercises.why: Single-leg curl with a stable, easy-to-load path.

exercises.name: Good morning
exercises.why: Long hamstring stretch, but hard on the lower back.

exercises.name: Nordic curl
exercises.why: Strong eccentric stimulus that is very hard to scale in small steps.

exercises.name: Glute-ham raise
exercises.why: Trains both hip and knee function, but needs special equipment.

exercises.name: Deep squat
exercises.why: Kubo et al. found full-depth squats grew the glutes more than half squats.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
exercises.why: Deep hip flexion under load on one leg at a time.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
exercises.why: Hips flexed under heavy load, shared with the hamstrings.

exercises.name: Hip thrust
exercises.why: Peak load at full hip extension; studies show glute growth similar to squats, not clearly more.

exercises.name: Walking lunge
exercises.why: Long steps and a forward lean bias the glutes.

exercises.name: Leg press (feet high)
exercises.why: A high foot position increases hip flexion under heavy, stable load.

exercises.name: 45° back extension
exercises.why: Rounding the upper back shifts the work from the spine to the glutes.

exercises.name: Hip abduction machine
exercises.why: Targets the upper glute (glute medius) with almost no fatigue.

exercises.name: Cable kickback
exercises.why: Light isolation finisher, hard to load progressively.

exercises.name: Standing calf raise
exercises.why: Kassiano et al. found reps in the stretched range grew the calves more; pause at the bottom.

exercises.name: Leg press calf raise
exercises.why: Heavy and stable, with an easy pause in the stretch.

exercises.name: Seated calf raise
exercises.why: The bent knee shifts the work to the soleus.

exercises.name: Smith calf raise
exercises.why: Stable bar; stand on a step for a full range.

exercises.name: Donkey calf raise
exercises.why: Bent hips with straight knees stretch the gastrocnemius further.

exercises.name: Single-leg dumbbell calf raise
exercises.why: Start with bodyweight, then add a dumbbell.

exercises.name: Cable crunch
exercises.why: Easy to load and progress like any other muscle.

exercises.name: Machine crunch
exercises.why: Stable, with small weight jumps.

exercises.name: Ab wheel rollout
exercises.why: Long stretch on the abs, but hard to scale.

exercises.name: Hanging leg raise
exercises.why: Curl the pelvis up rather than just lifting the legs.

exercises.name: Weighted decline crunch
exercises.why: Hold a plate to progress over time.

exercises.name: Reverse crunch
exercises.why: Bodyweight option that targets posterior pelvic tilt.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.why: A hold rather than reps; a weak growth stimulus.

exercises.name: Dead bug
exercises.why: Control drill with a low growth stimulus.
